model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 5 presents two line graphs side by side, both illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a specified threshold as a function of network layer depth, comparing conditions before and after applying gating mechanisms. The left graph uses a threshold of 1e-2, while the right graph uses a stricter threshold of 1e-3. Both graphs share identical axis labels and scales: the x-axis is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 20 in increments of 5, representing the depth of transformer layers; the y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio” and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, indicating the proportion of output values falling below the threshold. In both graphs, three distinct lines are plotted: a solid green line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate,” a dashed blue line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate,” and a dotted red line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate.” In the left graph (threshold 1e-2), the green line begins near 0.8 and declines steeply to approximately 0.2 by layer 20. The blue line starts near 0.6 and decreases to about 0.1, while the red line remains nearly flat near 0.0 across all layers. In the right graph (threshold 1e-3), the green line begins near 0.7 and declines to approximately 0.15; the blue line starts near 0.5 and drops to about 0.05; the red line again remains close to 0.0 throughout. All lines exhibit a general downward trend with increasing layer depth, with the “after gate” and “after average gate” conditions consistently showing lower sparsity ratios than the “before gate” condition. The graphs also include numerical annotations indicating the average sparsity ratio across all layers for each condition.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 5 presents two line charts side by side, both plotting the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a specified threshold as a function of network layer, comparing conditions before and after applying gating. The x-axis in both charts is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to approximately 22, with major tick marks at intervals of 5, indicating a linear scale representing discrete layer indices. The y-axis in both charts is labeled “Sparsity Ratio” and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, also on a linear scale. In the left chart (threshold 1e-2), the “sparsity ratio before gate” (green line with circle markers, solid) begins near 0.9 at layer 0 and declines sharply to below 0.1 by layer 5, remaining low through layer 22. The “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.64” (blue line with square markers, dashed) starts near 0.7, drops to approximately 0.2 by layer 5, and fluctuates slightly around 0.2–0.3 through layer 22. The “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33” (red line with triangle markers, dotted) begins near 0.4, declines to below 0.1 by layer 5, and remains near 0.1 through layer 22. In the right chart (threshold 1e-3), the “sparsity ratio before gate” (green line with circle markers, solid) starts near 0.8, drops to below 0.1 by layer 5, and stays low. The “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126” (blue line with square markers, dashed) begins near 0.6, falls to approximately 0.1 by layer 5, and remains around 0.1. The “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.089” (red line with triangle markers, dotted) starts near 0.3, drops to below 0.1 by layer 5, and remains near 0.1 through layer 22. All lines exhibit steep declines in sparsity ratio within the first five layers, followed by relative stability.
model_annotations.English: Figure 5 presents two line plots illustrating the proportion of SDPA output values below a specified threshold after applying gating, with the left plot using a threshold of 1e-2 and the right plot using 1e-3. Both plots share the same x-axis labeled “Layer,” ranging from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and y-axis labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In the left plot (threshold 1e-2), the green line with square markers (“sparsity ratio before gate”) starts at approximately 0.95 and declines steeply to near 0.0 by layer 5, then remains flat. The blue line with circle markers (“sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.64”) begins at ~0.95, drops sharply to ~0.3 by layer 5, and then gradually decreases to ~0.1 by layer 20. The red line with triangle markers (“sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33”) starts at ~0.95, falls to ~0.2 by layer 5, and remains relatively flat near 0.2 through layer 20. In the right plot (threshold 1e-3), the green line (“before gate”) begins at ~0.85, drops rapidly to near 0.0 by layer 5, and stays flat. The blue line (“after gate, avg 0.126”) starts at ~0.85, declines to ~0.1 by layer 5, and continues to decrease gradually to ~0.05 by layer 20. The red line (“after average gate, avg 0.089”) begins at ~0.85, drops to ~0.05 by layer 5, and remains nearly constant through layer 20. The plots also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states, as noted in the caption.
